name: Tesla Powerwall 3
fit: A home wanting solar and storage in a coordinated system, particularly on a single-phase supply.
why: Each unit provides 13.5 kWh of energy you can use, with separate expansion units for more storage.
check: One unit does not back up three phases. Confirm the gateway, configured output and compatibility with any existing solar or Powerwall.

sources.title: Powerwall 3 Australian technical specifications
sources.revision: Online manual; revision not displayed in extracted page

sources.title: Powerwall backwards compatibility
sources.revision: Current online guidance requires software 26.26 or later for stated PW2/PW3 combination

name: Sigenergy SigenStor with BAT 10.0 modules
fit: A home wanting expandable storage, with solar and optional EV equipment managed together.
why: Storage can be built from modules. The current AU warranty gives 9 kWh available to use per BAT 10.0 module.
check: Confirm backup circuits and internet-related warranty conditions. An official recall names older 8/10/12 kW single-phase controllers; check the exact model and serial, rather than treating every SigenStor as affected.

sources.title: Current AU/NZ SigenStor warranty
sources.revision: Revised 26 May 2026; current AU warranty page uploaded file 8 October 2026

name: Fox ESS CQ7 modular battery
fit: A home with measured evening demand large enough to justify substantial storage.
why: The current Australian CQ7 modules offer storage in 6.96 kWh steps; six give 41.76 kWh available to use.
check: The connected inverter still limits what can run at once. Confirm backup power on each phase and the exact CQ7 model; a larger battery does not automatically cover the whole home.

name: Fox ESS EP12 Plus (w)
fit: A home wanting storage in larger packs with a compatible Fox system.
why: Each current Australian pack provides 11.52 kWh available to use, with supported expansion across multiple packs.
check: Each pack weighs 98 kg. Confirm mounting, location, inverter compatibility and whether the quoted pack includes cold-weather heating.

name: Sungrow SBR
fit: A home using a compatible Sungrow inverter and wanting smaller storage steps.
why: Stackable 3.2 kWh modules help match storage to your actual evening use.
check: Not every module count works with every inverter. Confirm the allowed stack, backup switch and household power output.

sources.title: SBR manufacturer product page with AU region

name: Sungrow SBH
fit: A larger or increasingly electric home whose bills or meter data show substantial later-day use.
why: The range offers 15 to 40 kWh of storage in one stack, with 5 kWh module steps.
check: Extra storage does not guarantee extra power on one phase. Check the inverter and the exact battery revision's cold-weather behaviour.

name: Enphase IQ Battery 5P with FlexPhase
fit: An existing Enphase solar owner, or someone wanting storage built in 5 kWh steps.
why: The family supports designed single- or three-phase configurations with coordinated monitoring.
check: Quoted output is shared across the configured system; it is not the same output on every phase. Confirm the system controller and existing-solar behaviour in a blackout.

name: sonnen sonnenBatterie Evo
fit: An existing-solar owner wanting an integrated battery for selected essential circuits.
why: The Australian system lists 10 kWh available to use and built-in backup capability.
check: Ask which appliances it will run and whether the exact existing solar inverter can recharge it during a blackout.

name: sonnen sonnenBatterie 12
fit: A home considering new solar or retaining existing solar while adding coordinated storage.
why: The Australian range supports both new-panel and existing-inverter connections, with modular storage.
check: Backup is for a designed set of circuits. Confirm energy available to use, power output and the exact supported solar equipment.

name: BYD Battery-Box Premium HVM with BCU 2.0
fit: A home wanting a battery with a choice of supported inverter brands.
why: The current Australian HVM range offers expandable towers and publishes an inverter compatibility list.
check: Choose the inverter and module count together. Battery power and efficiency figures do not equal power and efficiency at household sockets.

sources.title: HVM/HVS BCU2 current Australian warranty
sources.revision: V1.1, 9 October 2026 listed on current manufacturer downloads page; terms not fully extracted here

name: GoodWe Lynx Home F G2
fit: A home with, or choosing, a supported GoodWe storage inverter.
why: Modules add storage in 3.2 kWh steps, with fault information available through the inverter.
check: Maximum storage differs by inverter model. Check the allowed stack and location; the current sheet does not support charging below freezing.

name: GoodWe ESA single-phase all-in-one
fit: A single-phase home wanting coordinated solar, storage and backup controls.
why: The current Australian range offers different controller outputs and compatible storage modules for expansion.
check: Its 63 A bypass figure describes grid power passing through, not battery output in a blackout. Get the actual backup power for the quoted controller.

name: AlphaESS SMILE-G3-S5 / SMILE-G3-B5
fit: A single-phase home wanting a clearly specified new-solar system or battery addition.
why: The Australian brochure separates the S5 for new solar from the B5 for an existing-solar addition.
check: A larger storage stack still shares a 5 kW controller. Confirm the exact module and usable energy; do not assume announced three-phase models are available.

sources.title: SMILE G3 BAT-10.1P datasheet
sources.revision: V08, 1 June 2023; applies to named older module only

name: SolarEdge Home Battery 400V
fit: A home already using, or choosing, a supported SolarEdge inverter and monitoring system.
why: The battery connects within SolarEdge's inverter and control system, with supported expansion.
check: A connected battery is not proof of blackout cover. The Australian page requires specified single-phase equipment and a Backup Interface for its stated backup design.

sources.title: SolarEdge Australian Home Battery 400V product page

name: Growatt APX HV Battery S2
fit: A home choosing a compatible Growatt storage inverter and modular battery.
why: The Australian downloads distinguish the APX variants, making the specified system combination important.
check: S0, S1, S2 and newer versions are not interchangeable. Have the installer identify the supported controller and module combination.

name: Growatt ALP LV E2
fit: A home whose specified inverter supports this Growatt battery family.
why: Storage grows in 5 kWh steps, with a weather-resistant enclosure.
check: Storage expansion does not keep increasing power output. The current battery sheet caps rated output at 6.5 kW for larger configurations, before any inverter limit.

name: BYD Battery-Box Premium LVS
fit: A home using a supported inverter, including a professionally designed off-grid system.
why: The Australian sheet provides 4 kWh usable modules with published inverter configuration rules.
check: Larger towers cannot all be connected in parallel. Have the installer confirm allowed expansion, cabling and cold-weather charging.

name: SolaX TSYS-HS51
fit: A home with a supported SolaX storage inverter that needs room for future storage growth.
why: The Australian-listed family offers a wide modular storage range.
check: The headline size exceeds the energy available to use. Confirm module versions and accessories; a feature labelled coming soon is not included equipment.

fit: A single-phase home wanting coordinated solar, storage and selected-circuit backup.
why: The Australian company provides monitoring, firmware updates and documented backup output for the system.
check: More storage does not increase its 5 or 6 kW backup output. Confirm the exact compatible battery revision and written local service arrangements.

name: SAJ HS3 single-phase AU
fit: A single-phase home wanting integrated storage in 5 kWh steps.
why: The Australian sheet identifies local controllers and modules, including their backup output.
check: The general page and Australian sheet show different expansion limits. Confirm the quoted configuration and actual warranty policy.
